title: The Forest Where Storms Grow as Trees

features.name: oldest storm-trunk
features.desc-on-touch: A tree grown from lightning. Its rings count not years but thunderstorms. It is patient and angry at the same time.

features.name: rain-root tangle
features.desc-on-touch: Roots that learned to grow from water itself. They tie the whole forest together, remembering every deluge.

features.name: hail-shatter grove
features.desc-on-touch: Where small trees were shaped by ice and now grow twisted, teaching their younger siblings how to bend without breaking.

features.name: lightning scar
features.desc-on-touch: A long white mark down bark where the storm wrote its signature. The tree healed around it, incorporating the scar into its rings.

features.name: wind-learned canopy
features.desc-on-touch: A crown of branches that negotiated with the storm, learning to flex instead of resist. The forest speaks in the language of wind.

features.name: sediment's memory
features.desc-on-touch: The forest floor holds every storm that made it. Layers of debris, ash, and regrowth. You walk on compressed history.

reverie.title: REVERIE — in the rain-cave of an old storm-tree
narr: You are both pressed into the hollow of this tree during
heavy rain, and the rain on bark sounds like applause. She
is tracing the lightning scar with her fingertip, and she
says: this tree survived what we carry. You understand then:
the forest doesn't heal its wounds. It grows around them,
makes them part of the shape it was always meant to be.

inscription: every tree here is an argument with the sky that never ended and learned to keep living anyway
